assertion_audit.failure_condition: crew.complete stops releasing a landed tree, or the fixture's landing leaves the tree unreleasable; the assertion reads the promotion's own report, not the fixture's expectation.
The published snapshot loses the row, which would make the empty stdout below a statement about the snapshot instead of about the hook.
The hook's recheck stops dropping a released row; mutation-recheck-disabled.log reproduces exactly this red with the recheck returning early.
The derivation stops holding a tree that still carries the run's own unlanded commit.
The tree-absence half of the recheck stops dropping the row; it is red in mutation-recheck-disabled.log alongside :314.
An absent per-run file stops keeping the duty, or the aggregate ledger is consulted instead of the per-run file.
A recorded release stops deciding, so a row survives where the ledger record says the tree was released.

assertion_independence: No added assertion compares a value against the same variable the test handed in: tests/test_a_worktree_held_row_is_rechecked_at_read.py:300 reads crew.complete's own report, :307 and :310 read a payload derived by the production obligations view from the fixture ledger, :338 compares the fixture tree path against git's own `worktree list` output, and :357 asserts against ledger.run_path's own resolution.
